intro.title: :nth-child and :not()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a styled list where you'll highlight specific items and exclude others using CSS selectors. You'll learn how to use the :nth-child() pseudo-class to target elements based on their position, such as every other row or a specific number. You'll also use the :not() pseudo-class to apply styles to all elements except those matching a given selector. This involves writing CSS rules to create visual patterns and exclusions in your HTML structure. By the end, you'll understand how to combine these selectors for precise styling control.
intro.usecase: The :nth-child and :not() selectors are essential for styling complex, data-driven interfaces. Developers use :nth-child to create zebra-striped tables in dashboards, highlight every third product in an e-commerce grid, or style alternate rows in admin panels for better readability. Meanwhile, :not() is crucial for applying styles broadly while excluding specific elements, such as styling all form inputs except submit buttons, or targeting list items except the first one in a navigation menu. These selectors help build clean, maintainable CSS for interactive UIs like data tables, filterable galleries, and dynamic form layouts.
